target.name: Human dipeptidyl peptidase IV / CD26 (DPP-4)
target.reference: Liang GB et al. Bioorg Med Chem Lett. 2008;18(13):3706-3710. doi:10.1016/j.bmcl.2008.05.061

safety_panel.note: four-chain channel; docking is a flag, not a verdict

library.docking_note: 62 stereoisomer duplicates of docked parent structures were not docked

reference_ligand_redocking.rmsd_note: see redocking_results.csv for the RMSD per protein

project_title: Computational Screening of Neem-Associated Natural Products Against Human DPP-4
biological_rationale: DPP-4 degrades the incretin hormones GLP-1 and GIP, which contribute to glucose regulation. Inhibition of DPP-4 prolongs incretin activity and is an established therapeutic strategy for type 2 diabetes.
drug_discovery_rationale: Identify neem-associated natural products with potentially favourable predicted interactions with human DPP-4 through computational screening.

selectivity_norm.description: Normalised computational selectivity assessment involving hERG, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6

admet_score.description: Combined drug-likeness and computational ADMET assessment

definitions_checked_against_files.efficacy_norm: min-max of the DPP-4 Vina score over all 238 docked compounds; reconstructed from the delivered files
definitions_checked_against_files.selectivity_norm: min-max over the top 10 of the worst (most negative) difference between a safety-protein score and the DPP-4 score; reconstructed from the delivered files, confirm with the ML engineer

limitations: Docking scores represent computational predictions and do not establish experimental binding or enzyme inhibition.
Computational selectivity scores do not establish biological selectivity or safety.
Botanical provenance and exact compound identities require confirmation against primary literature.
No experimental DPP-4 inhibition results are reported.
proposed_next_steps: Verify shortlisted compound structures and botanical provenance.
Inspect and validate predicted protein-ligand binding poses.
Conduct in-vitro DPP-4 enzyme inhibition assays.
Prioritise promising compounds for further medicinal chemistry investigation.
